ratings_why.fun: One small verb (Reforge, +1/+1) that every card reads, plus four builds that pull the same cards different ways; I'd happily draft it, though the Heat maths gets heavy late.
ratings_why.distinct: Scorch that you carry into the next fight and Regrow that halves itself are fresh; Reforge-as-anywhere-+1/+1 with a counter cards read feels close to familiar gem tribes.

verdict_why: Every card now reads as written and the v1 clarity problems are fixed; more passes would change it, not improve it.

points.text: Each unit carries Attack, Health, Scorch and Heat at once. The card face needs a distinct Heat pip and burn marks for Scorch, or the board stops reading at a glance.
Bellows-Boy's 'spend up to 2, always as much as you have' reads in two passes. 'End of Turn: spend 2 gold (or 1 if that's all you have)' says the same thing faster.

Mother Atra's fantasy is patience, carrying young for years, but her card is a burst of Attack on comebacks. A slow card, such as growing each turn a unit keeps its Scorch, would let the flavour show in play.

Crested Konrad's 'to the right of this' is plain, but the crest and courtship don't show in what he does. Passing Heat to the unit beside him could read as a display, if the name or art leans into it.
Nutrisco is the tribe's loudest card, but empty slots don't tie to 'I nourish and extinguish'. Something like 'feeds on what you sold' would make the motto do the work.

standouts.why: Smooth Tobias tells the whole tribe on a Tier 1 card: heat it every turn and it comes back after dying. The regrown-tail joke is in the rules.
Ember-Belly Newt reads instantly and makes the Burn to Rise combo with Ottilie: burn your own unit on purpose so it comes back stronger.
Wet Cellar Keeper puts the secret wet cellar into play: heal the burns, keep the Health. The card text now shows when it goes.

weakest.why: Mother Atra's text is fine, but her flavour (patience) and her effect (burst on Regrow) don't match.
Crested Konrad does a useful job, moving Heat, but it's the least woodland-feeling card and its flavour stays in the name.
Fumarole Spitter scales off one unit's Heat, so a T3 ping card quietly turns into dozens of pings late; players will misjudge it from the shop.

flags.note: +1/+1 per Heat for each empty slot can reach +90/+90 in fight; the designer already flags it for a sim.
At 30 Heat it fires 30 random pings at Start of Combat from a Tier 3 slot.
Gain per Reforge grows with Heat and Heat grows with Reforges; quadratic, as the designer notes.
